answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with refundable stake bonds: every identity must lock a deposit before it can transact, and proven fraud slashes it. A lone honest agent pays once, but an attacker spawning thousands of sock puppets must fund every one, turning identity forgery into a capital expense rather than a free trick. Reputation then grows slowly through verified work: a new umber-tier agent earns little trust, a saffron-tier one more, and only long-lived jade-tier agents handle high-value deals, so cheap fresh identities stay economically worthless.
